utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you have the accused come into the courtroom? The accused will be testifying. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good afternoon to the interpreters. I want to be sure that everybody can hear me. Does everybody hear? Good afternoon to the Defence and Prosecution counsel, to the court reporters, and to General Blaskic. General Blaskic is going to continue with his testimony, that is, continue with the examination-in-chief being conducted by Mr. Nobilo. I am saying this for everybody here who doesn't know. I would like to explain. This is the examination-in-chief of the Defence, and the Defence wanted the accused to testify. Let me remind the accused that, as a witness, he has taken an oath, and that he is still under oath. Good afternoon. You may now begin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If you will recall, at the end of last week, we started talking about the special purpose units and their chain of command, and since this was really -- this was opened at the very end of the day on Friday, General, would you just say again to remind us, could you list these special purposes units and what their purposes were and how they differed from the brigades which you commanded over?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, the special purpose units were as follows: The Convicts or Penal Battalion, Ante Bruno Busic Battalion, the Ludwig Pavlovic Battalion, the Alpha Force Battalion, the Vitezovi, the Tvrtko unit, the Apostles. These units were established as an integral part of the defence department of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and they were not linked or bound to a territory. This was pursuant to the -- and on the basis of orders issued by the Ministry of the Defence, they could have been deployed in any part of the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. None of these units were ever part of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone structure and its organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say by orders of the head of the defence department who later became the Minister of Defence, are you saying that these units were subordinated to the civilian authorities or to the main staff?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These units were subordinated exclusively to the civilian part of the defence department. They were never under the command of the main headquarters of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This model of military units not being under the command of the soldiers but under the civilian authorities, are you aware of any such model anywhere, either in the JNA or any other model that you may have studied?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Up until then, I had never heard of such a model, and I couldn't reconcile myself to such manner of organising of military structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At some stage, more precisely, sometime around the 9th of January, 1993, two of such units, the special purpose units who previously had not operated in Central Bosnia, did appear there. These were the Bruno Busic and the Ludwig Pavlovic units.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know how they arrived at this territory, on whose request and who sent them there, and did you take part in their coming to Central Bosnia in any way?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that from the 13th of November, 1992, the entire combat commands in the area of Travnik and Novi Travnik were taken over by the joint command of the BH army and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone of the HVO, and the headquarters of this joint command was in Plave Vode in Travnik. Messrs. Prkacin and Pasalic ["Pavlovic" in real-time transcript], who were commanders of the joint command, insisted to get intervention units for the defence of Travnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just a moment. For the transcript, it says that these were Prkacin and Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, Prkacin and Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just to remind the Trial Chamber, Pasalic was an officer with the army of Bosnia and Herzogovina.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was with the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the lead man in the joint command for the 3rd Corps on behalf of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. At the request of the joint command, these units were sent by the defence department in Mostar to Novi Travnik and to Vitez, and the command over these units, including the right to use them in combat, was conferred to the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell me, in specific situations, could it be the case that you would issue commands to a special purpose unit, let's say to the Vitezovi unit who were frequently in your territory, and if so, under what circumstances and how was this done?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Again, I could not reconcile myself to this type of organisation, and I tried to inform my superiors of this, and there were also situations when I wanted and thought that I needed to inform the Vitezovi and other units about the activities of the HVO brigades in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Sometimes this was oral information, sometimes it would be sent as an information from the headquarters, but overall, my position was the position of the coordinator of these forces. In any situation, the commander of the Vitezovi could have a discretionary position in respect to my orders, which meant that he could carry out these orders or inform me that I did not have the authority, that is, that I was not competent to issue orders to the special purpose units. I received this position in writing on the 5th of January, 1993, from the Vitezovi commander. In this memo, he expressed the position that the Central Bosnia Operative Zone did not have the authority to issue him orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Later on we will return to these issues, but now that we are focusing on the special purpose units, can you explain to the Trial Chamber what the word "subordination" means? That means the units which were not directly subordinated to you were turned over to your authority for special combat operations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In terms of the chain of command, which means that there are certain rules whereby a superior command can reinforce certain subordinate units with additional units, and during the period in which these combat operations are carried out, such reinforcements are subordinated to the commander of the overall operation. The higher command, the superior command, reserves the right to define the extent to which such a unit will be subordinated, how long this subordination is going to last, and what the authority of the commander of the overall combat operation will be with respect to this subordinated unit. However, this subordinated unit is not part of the manpower under the command of these subordinated commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: After, let's say, a battle is over, what happens between you and this subordinated unit which is not under your command?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The situation is reversed to the previous state of affairs, which means that I still have no authority, that is, control and command of this unit, and that this unit continues to be in the chain of command directly subordinated to the higher command. If these are the special purpose units, this would then mean that the Ministry of Defence has the authority of command and control over this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At this point in your testimony, can we just, for orientation, give the example of Grbavica where you de facto did have command over the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is a good example. This was a case when I commanded this unit, but the commander of this unit still has freedom to decide what forces and what means he was going to employ to carry out these tasks because he was aware of the fact that I was not competent to -- for instance, do not provide him the logistics to discipline him if such a task was not carried out and I, on my part, was aware that it was very difficult to foresee the behaviour of such units during the combat. However, in the given situation, I had no other choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let's now leave aside the special purpose unit issues even though we will come back to it later on. I would like to take you to a new area which I thought that we would discuss today, which means that I want to take you to the organisational work which you carried out in January of 1993. Did you continue with the process of transformation of the armed villages into an army? If you did so, can you just give us some pointers, what is it that you did in this part of January before you had the conflict on the 25th of January with the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I continued with my activities regarding organisation and establishment of an army from these armed villages, so that as early as the end of November of 1992, we renamed the municipal staffs into HVO brigades. On the 9th of January, 1993, I was working on drafting the mobilisation documents as a proposal, and these documents included the mobilisation plans and registration sheets for every single soldier. This was work on setting up the basic files for the military conscripts. These are tasks which really fall within the ambit of the Ministry of Defence, but we did this work because we had no other documents. On the 11th of January, 1993, I was working on a draft of the establishment of the home guard on the basis of a decree on home guard, and I tried to establish a structure of local units of home guard which would be based in a specific territory and would basically be static units. As in early December the chief of staff of the Operative Zone was involved in this work, in January of 1993, we drafted a first plan of monitoring of the immediately subordinate command posts and units of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What is the role of monitoring within the command and control?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is one of the basic functions of any command in order to identify the distinction between the ordered and the implemented actions in order to gain an insight into how the orders were implemented on the ground, and after certain orders were issued, an analysis was carried out to ascertain how much it was carried out in order to then issue additional orders which would be corrective orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you add what other measures you took in order to convert the armed villagers into the army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sometime in mid January, we drafted a form in which we tried to establish certain rules about replacements and shifts of men, of personnel, on the front lines. We tried to provide more stability and regularity in these operations and provide for stability of the front line at the time of the change of shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How did you organise the artillery?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As early as the period when the joint command took over the command, that is, the joint command of the 3rd Corps and the Operative Zone, the entire artillery was under the command of the joint command. It was organised in such a way that the crews, who manned these artillery pieces and armaments in their emplacements, were mixed. That means they consisted of the members of the HVO and the BH army members. The commanders of the artillery had an office in which they jointly made plans about the activities and work of the joint command. These commanders were from both the HVO and the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 14th of January, 1993, you held a meeting with all brigade commanders from the Operative Zone, almost all, and this was just to further this work, and could you just briefly say, what did you identify as the burning problems or burning issues in each of the municipalities within the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had a meeting with the commanders. The problems were several, and let me mention some. As far as the Travnik Brigade is concerned, 300 soldiers were being replaced on a daily basis on 400 kilometres of front line against the Serbs. These were soldiers from the neighbouring municipalities who were carrying out their tasks at the Travnik front. In Novi Travnik, there was a lot of shelling at the front line by the Serbs. We had difficulties with shifts in Novi Travnik because the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, at their checkpoints, impeded the passage of the shifts. I was also informed that in Novi Travnik there had been some acts of provocation, and within the HVO, it was the Ante Bruno Busic Regiment, that is, a special purpose unit, which did most of that, and on the Bosniak Muslim side, it was members of the 308th Mountain Brigade. We had one serious incident in Novi Travnik where an HVO checkpoint was attacked by the Novi Travnik units of the BH army. The location of this checkpoint was at Medenik. The brigade commander from Zenica reported that there were a number of murders and suicides in his zone of responsibility; further, that members of the green legion, who were part of the 314th Brigade of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, were attacking Croats which caused fear among the Croatian population in Zenica. I was informed that the military police in Zenica had employed 15 policemen who had criminal records and that members of HOS in Zenica, who are also part of the 314th Brigade of the BH army, were pressuring Croats there. In Kiseljak, there were problems of control and command as well and the impossibility of having -- the new commander could not take over the command from the old commander. In Busovaca, the commander had asked for the dismantling of the entire military police because it was full of criminals. The commander from Vares, another case in point, said that he had had difficulties with regard to sending soldiers to the Travnik front to fight against the Serbs. The commander from Zepce reported about the upset relations that existed between them and members of the HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned Kiseljak and said that there was a problem there over handing over duties of one commander to another. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber, sometime in mid January 1993, you undertook a drive to replace commanders in three municipalities. Could you tell us your motives for this? Who did you wish to replace and who did you wish to put in the place of the commanders you were replacing?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wanted to bring, in three municipalities, that is, Kiseljak, Busovaca, and Novi Travnik, new commanders there, and in order to do so, I wrote proposals to the chief of the main staff, I sent him my proposals, and the representative of the defence department. I was motivated in doing this, and I wanted to bring commanders who would be loyal to the command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, that is to say, commanders who would not have had on their shoulders previous incidents or the conflicts that we had with the BH army beforehand, who were not burdened with that kind of event and incident, commanders who would be tolerant in their behaviour and conduct, commanders who were professionally and militarily the best experts in the field, the ones who we had available, and the representative of the defence department gave his permission for these commanders to be replaced in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who did you want to send to the municipalities, and did you hold negotiations and agreements? Who were the new commanders in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Novi Travnik, after the conflict in October 1992, the local commander was replaced of the municipal headquarters of the Croatian Defence Council, Vlado Juric, and the man who replaced him was Borivoje Malbasic, he became the new commander, from Vares. In Busovaca, Dusko Grubesic was the commander who was relieved of his duties, and he was replaced by the new commander who was Mr. Niko Jozinovic from Zepce. In Kiseljak, a commander who was to have been replaced, Commander Ivica Rajic, according to the documents, he received an order relieving him of his duties and to hand over his duties to somebody else, to the new commander, and the new commander was to have been Mr. Mijo Bozic who performed the duty, who worked in the headquarters of the Operative Zone. However, we had difficulties. I personally had difficulties in Kiseljak itself because this replacement did not take place because all the representatives of the civilian authorities, despite the consultations that I had previously had, retained their attitude and stood firm in their attitude and did not allow this replacement to take place, that is to say, the replacement between Rajic and Bozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who did you hold a meeting with in the aim of replacing the commander?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 19th of January, 1993, after 3.00 p.m., I had a meeting with the representatives of the civilian authorities from Kiseljak, that is to say, the mayor of Kiseljak, the president of the HDZ party in Kiseljak, the members of the municipal government at Kiseljak, and the meeting was also attended by Mr. Rajic and Mr. Mijo Bozic. The topic of the meeting was the replacement of the two commanders and the hand-over of duties. I tried to convince them that the order by the defence minister was such that it had to be carried out and that it was necessary to implement the order. The discussion lasted until almost midnight, and I received a declarative okay from the members of the meeting; namely, the members said that this hand-over of duty would take place in the ensuing period. It was to have taken place by the 10th of January; however, this hand-over of duty was not completed even by the 23rd of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We'll speak about the state of affairs in Kiseljak later on and this official hand-over of duty, but I would just like to ask you whether this is normal for an army. Is it normal for you to negotiate with the representative of the HDZ, the municipal authorities, and have meetings from 3.00 p.m. until midnight? Was that standard procedure? In any kind of serious army, would that be standard procedure?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was not standard procedure. It is not standard procedure in any army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us now move on to another area, and before we go on to discuss the conflict in January between the HVO and the BH army, can you tell us something about the security situation in the territory of the Novi Travnik, Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca, and Kiseljak municipalities, and public law and order, how was that enforced, just the gist of it, the main outline?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Law and order was upset in January 1993. This process continued, especially in the municipalities of Novi Travnik, Travnik, and Vitez. The form that this disruption of law and order took was that whole shifts would be taken prisoner, that is, all the shifts along the front lines towards the Serbs and anybody moving around the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who would take whom prisoner?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The BH army in Kruscica, on the 27th of January, 1993, took a whole shift of the members of the Croatian Defence of Vitez prisoner, including a motor vehicle that they had and that these soldiers had to take them to the front, so they took everybody prisoner and confiscated the vehicles, the weapons, and everything else. Then there was an incident which took place on the 13th of January in Kakanj where the BH army expelled the military police of the Croatian Defence Council from the town of Kakanj itself. There were other incidents as well linked to the taking of prisoners. The HVO, for example, and the members of these special purposes unit, were foremost among them, and the HVO soldiers would be arrested by the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say the PPN, you're referring to the special purposes units, are you not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In order to throw more light on this new element in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia that we have introduced, I should like to show you some documents, Defence Exhibits 204, 206, 208, so they are Exhibits D204, 206, and 208. I am going to read you the document number D204, which is on the ELMO, some key points from that document. It is dated the 25th of January, 1993, and it is the 2nd Battalion which is reporting on the activities of groups and individuals acting without the knowledge of the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council command. "Serious problems in the Vitez municipality are made by groups and individuals which, in their uniforms and with HVO insignia, are pilfering socially-owned property and very frequently private property. During the robberies, they have made use of all forms of criminal activity. "Their main objective is to loot, however, as nobody is making an effort to put an end to this, their criminal offences put an additional strain on the already tense inter-ethnic relations. Lately, local robbers have been cooperating with soldiers from Herzegovina who have become emboldened, and the Herzegovinis have been trying to loot privately-owned buildings themselves." And then the document goes on to quote examples. Could you tell us, please, reports of this kind, did they reach you, and if so, in what way did you react to them? In what way could you react to them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Reports of this kind did reach me, and this was just one report from the 2nd Battalion of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade from Vitez. The brigade had two other battalions at the time, one in Novi Travnik, and I asked the commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade to try and do his utmost to maintain a dialogue with the commander of the 308th Brigade of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina from Novi Travnik and by means of holding meetings to try and solve the problems that existed and the incidents that took place. I issued an order to that effect, banning any long weapons to be bandied about in the town of Novi Travnik, and this was for soldiers, members of the HVO, and I asked the security officer to spend some time in Novi Travnik himself and to do what he could to undertake preventive measures to stop incidents of this kind, and in this particular report, one can note that the local looters were encouraged with the activities of the soldiers themselves, soldiers from Herzegovina, and the report mentions the Herzegovins, who were, in fact, members of the special purposes units who, through their own activities, contributed to the chaotic state of affairs that existed in the region. All I could do was to prevail upon their commanders, to call upon them to say that all this was not in keeping with the law and that it was a very bad thing that things like this were happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were you able to take any disciplinary measures towards the soldiers from Herzegovina, members of the special purposes units?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that was not within my power and authority. I was not able to take any disciplinary measures against those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because those particular units were not within the organic formation of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. They were under the competencies of the defence department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before we continue, I should like to read out another document on the same subject. It is Defence Exhibit D206. So can we have that placed on the ELMO now, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am going to read this out. The document is dated the 13th of January, 1993. It is from the 2nd Vitez Battalion. The title is "Report on Security in the 2nd Vitez Battalion," and I'm going to read point number 2. "The newly-arrived HVO units from Herzegovina are causing us great difficulties. Every evening, they walk around the town with weapons and disturb the citizens by firing bursts of gunfire while intoxicated. This problem is all the more serious because of the school classes that are going on in Vitez, which means that there are many children on the streets. We are frightened that an even more serious incident could occur as a result of this shooting." And so on and so forth. I'm not going to read it any further. "There was also an attempt to take a car from our chief of communications, Zoran Jukic." Tell us, please, descriptions of this kind that your subordinates sent to you, subordinate officers, do you feel that they could have caused fear amongst the Muslims because they were incidents perpetrated by the Croats?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course, and they did instil fear with the Bosniak Muslim population where these units were based.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I should like to read sections of another document that you yourself wrote. It is Defence Exhibit 208, and it is related to these units from Herzegovina. Could the third document be placed on the ELMO, please? On the 6th of February, 1993, you wrote a warning, due to the failure to carry out command number 01-1-217/93, dating from the 10th of January, 1993, and it is addressed to all HVO brigades in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and to the independent units, the OZ SB, and the text reads as follows. "By command number 01-1-217/93, from the 18th of January, 1993 --" There is obviously a misprint there because the order was the 18th of January, 1993. " -- and in connection with repeated occurrences of the disturbance of public law and order, murders, injuries, threats with firearms, opening fire in inhabited places as well as a worsening of the entire security situation, concrete duties have been established to counteract such negative acts and proceedings. "Since until today adequate and efficient measures have not been taken, but the aforesaid negativities have been vented to a large extent, I W A R N - All commanders of brigades and independent units in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone of their duty to carry out the aforesaid commands. By 8 February 1993, this Command Headquarters is to be informed in writing about the measures and actions taken pursuant to this command." It is signed Commander Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. You sent this warning to the HVO brigades and to the 4th LARD of the PZO, to the 4th Vitez Battalion, and so on and so forth. Quite obviously, the Herzegovina Brigade was not there at the time. Tell me now, please, did this order represent one of the measures that you took in order to try and put the situation right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This order reflects the situation that existed at the time because following an overall order from the 18th of January, 1993, a comprehensive order that was sent out, instead of stopping a deterioration in the security situation, upsetting law and order, what happened was that law and order was upset even further, and that is why I was obliged to send out this warning, once again demanding that orders be put into effect. The units from Herzegovina had already left because, already in January 1993, at meetings with the joint commands, I insisted upon the fact that these units be sent away from the area of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone because, for a time, they were the perpetrators of the disorder that was going on, and I sent out a request in writing demanding the chief of the main staff and the head of the defence department to have these units, special purposes units from Herzegovina, withdrawn from the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, so that this could be an attempt at stabilising the security situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. If I might interrupt for a moment, before we move off this document, for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The witness just clarified a point, and I think it can be clarified just with a pen notation possibly by Mr. Dubuisson, and that has to do with Exhibit 208 which, candidly, I didn't notice until now. As you can see on the ELMO, the first line of that reads, "By the command number," whatever, "from 18 January, 1993," and as the witness rightly points out, the original carries with it the date of 18 January, as does the French version. I merely say that just so if we could note that and correct that in the English translation that's part of the record. Counsel, if you don't mind a pen notation, we certainly don't mind either.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is correct, and the Defence does not object to that because it is clear from the document that this was the 18th of January. However, the first mention of this order has not been printed very legibly, so this is what creates the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Be that as it may, I think it is an issue that we all can agree on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to take advantage of this interruption in order to make my own interruption. The French version was the only one, which is D208, the only one in French. The second paragraph, in my opinion, has an ambiguity, since this was translated into French. Of course, I cannot make a judgment in respect of the Serbo-Croatian version, but it seems to me that in respect of the English version, the nuance is an important one because in the French versions that I have in front of me -- I don't know whether you are the one who had this translated into French, Mr. Nobilo? Are you the one, or was it the registry service?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I believe that probably it was the registry who did this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. It was the registry that had this translated. All right. This is not someone who is trying to be a purist in the French language, but there is an ambiguity as to the sense. The witness said that in the second paragraph, "take into effect that the measures did not bear fruit," whereas the French version which I have in front of me says "express the negative qualities." I don't think it is a very good translation, but that is a very different sense. One has the impression that the accused took the order because criticisms had been expressed, whereas when the witness expressed himself, he said it's because it was not producing any results, objectively speaking. This is an important nuance. Did the witness take the order because it was criticised or because the results were not good? I'm noting what the witness said, but I would ask the registrar to have this document resubmitted to the translation unit, that is D208, especially the second paragraph, which is not only in poor French but, in my opinion, also displays an ambiguity. If you don't mind, Mr. Dubuisson, have this sent back to the translation department, please? Excuse me for having interrupted, but I wanted to take advantage of that moment, and as far as I'm concerned, I will stay with what the witness said. All right, Mr. Nobilo. You can go on for another ten minutes, and then we will take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are grateful because the gist of this is that the Colonel expresses his dissatisfaction and asks that something additional should be done precisely because the previous orders had not been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, let me now bring you back to the previous question. You asked that these units be withdrawn because of the violence, and you said that this was because of the security of the population. But as a commander, can you tell me, would experienced, well-armed, well-equipped units be of use to you in any type of combat situation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The position of the joint command and my position and the position of Dzemo Merdan was that these units were necessary for us in order for us to be able to defend ourselves in this territory, so they were of an exceptional military significance. But the problem was that we did not have adequate accommodations, that is, barracks where we would accommodate them at the time they were not engaged in combat operations and tasks. They did make a contribution to the stability of our defence lines; and on the battlefront, we usually did not have any kind of problems with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, they were deployed to combat the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, again, if I understand you correctly, you are sacrificing good combat units in order to improve the security?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to take you to a new area of questioning, which is the military situation which, during three weeks in January, would lead to the first conflict between the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is, the 3rd Corps, and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. The last time, that is, on Friday, you said that after a series of local incidents, the first thing that really concerned you was the spread of the BH army in what you call the depth of territory, that is, behind the front lines. Could you tell the Trial Chamber which units were those -- that is, the units of the BH army -- were beginning to be deployed in the depth of the territory, and what did that lead to later? If necessary, you could move closer to the model. Mr. President, with your agreement, maybe this would be a good moment to stop, and we could use the break in order to prepare the model with this new situation. I think that it would really speed up the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. All right. We will take a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume the hearing. Please be seated. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So we are now dealing with the development of the military situation on the eve of the first conflict between the 3rd Corps and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone in January of 1993. General, tell me, in late '92 and in January 1993, did you notice something that had raised your concerns, and the later developments will bear out this concern of yours?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, in late 1992, it was already noticeable that the BH army units were amassing behind the front lines in the depth of the territory which was under the control of the HVO and the BH army. As a commander, I was concerned about this at the time, and I spoke on several occasions with Dzemo and Enver, both commanders with the 3rd Corps, about these deployments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: "Dzemo" is Dzemo Merdan?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, "Dzemo" is Dzemo Merdan and "Enver" is Enver Hadzihasanovic, who were the commander and the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were talking about this amassing of forces in the depth of the territory, and with your permission, Your Honours, I would like to step forward and use the model.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. If Prosecution counsel wishes to do the same thing, they may do so. Could the witness express himself and speak clearly, please? All right. I think everybody is ready. Mr. Nobilo, please come closer. Can the public see as well? Can the camera be focused in such a way that the public gallery can see? All right. Very well. We can begin. Please proceed. Mr. Blaskic, the floor is yours. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The front line positions against the Serbs, which I am pointing to (indicating), is not accurate in geographical terms because we do not have all the features of the terrain. I am going to mention them, and later on, I can point to them on the map. What I'm pointing at right now is Travnik (indicating). This is the town of Novi Travnik (indicating). This is the highway leading from Novi Travnik (indicating) via Opara going to Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And then onward from Gornji Vakuf, where does this road go from there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It leads further to Prozor, Jablanica, and beyond in the direction of Mostar. The other road from Novi Travnik is in the direction that I'm pointing now (indicating), and it leads via Ravno Rostovo to Bugojno, and then due east from Bugojno to Gornji Vakuf, and again Prozor, Jablanica, and Mostar. The Serbian army controlled the following features: It was Mount Vlasic, the Radalj feature, the Komar feature. The 1st Krajina Corps from Banja Luka was deployed along this line (indicating) and parts of the 2nd Krajina Corps from the town of Titov Drvar. Facing these Serbian forces, in fact, we organised a joint defence against these Serbian forces in Travnik consisting of the HVO and the BH army, the Central Bosnia Operative Zone whose headquarters was in Vitez, and the 3rd Corps of the BH army headquartered in Zenica. The joint command was at Plave Vode, which I'm pointing at right now (indicating), and this joint command had taken over -- I'm just correcting the position here, Your Honours. This is the location of Plave Vode (indicating). This is what I'm pointing at now. So the joint command took over the complete command and control, including the combat engagement in Travnik as of 13 November, 1992. From the feature of Lupoglav all the way to Vlaska Gromila, which is where the front line was held by the HVO and the BH forces, and at the Lupoglav location, including from Lupoglav to Mescema, there were no BH army soldiers on the front line, except for several villages where there were some Mujahedeen forces, they were part of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and parts of the 312th Brigade, who had the role of providing combat security. The BH army had a more significant presence in Turbe. The Travnik defence was organised in sectors, in sector 1, which was the main area from the main Travnik-Turbe road to the right, and sector 2 was the area between the Travnik-Turbe highway and to the left. As far as the military situation is concerned, all combat activities were conducted over Vilenica feature. Had the Serbs taken Vilenica, the town of Travnik would have fallen. So my main concern in January of 1993 was the following: The main communication line between Novi Travnik and Herzegovina, which includes Novi Travnik, Gornji Vakuf, Prozor, Tomislavgrad, and beyond that Mostar, and the other, Novi Travnik, Ravno Rostovno, Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, Mostar, was occupied by the forces of the 308th Brigade of the BH army from Novi Travnik. So that means in the area which I'm pointing to now (indicating) and in this area here (indicating), the entire 308th Brigade was deployed, and in the area of Ravno Rostovo, a Mujahedeen unit from the 7th Muslim Brigade was deployed. These forces which were in the area of the main communication line and belonged to the BH army were not deployed on the defence lines of Novi Travnik but were deployed behind the front lines, in the depth of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the meaning of the existence of such large forces which were not engaged in the defence against the common enemy, that is, the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was the -- I was also giving an answer to this question from Mr. Dzemo Merdan at the time, the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, and from Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic at the meeting of the 21st of December, 1992 in Zenica. He answered that he was creating operative forces and that he wanted to have a trained and mobile army. I personally was concerned by the positioning of these forces because this was not an exception but a practice which was also implemented in other areas. The meaning of it was that you achieve monitoring and control of the communications, and all communications lines are of strategic significance in any war, and in mountainous terrain, such as in Bosnia-Herzegovina, especially in Central Bosnia, they are of vital importance. The next brigade was the 306th Brigade of the BH army which was headquartered in Han Bila, and its operations were going due north along the road Han Bila-Metkovic, and the command post of the brigade itself and its barracks was, as you can see from this model, on the only road from Travnik via Guca Gora and Han Bila, Stranjani, Cajdras, to Zenica. So if we wanted to take the road from Travnik to Zenica, this is the road that takes you to Zenica, and this is the main communication line. In addition to the 306th Brigade in Han Bila, another brigade was being formed in Mehuric, and I'm pointing to that location on the model here (indicating). It is not exactly here. It is beyond what is represented on the model here. And the 27th Krajina Brigade was composed of mostly Bosniak Muslims who were expelled from Banja Luka. In the town of Travnik itself, the 17th Krajina Brigade was stationed, a mobile brigade, which also was composed of the Bosnian refugees from Sanski Most and Prijedor, and it was deployed in the Travnik barracks. Further in Travnik, there were forces of the Mujahedeen from the 7th Muslim Brigade to the strength of a battalion, and the BH army unit, alongside the HVO forces, was manning the defence lines in Travnik. The next unit was the 325th Brigade of the BH army in Vitez which had its forces organised in battalions. One battalion was deployed in Kruscica, I believe it was the 2nd Battalion; another battalion in Poculica with companies in Poculica and Vrhovine, that is, Prnjavor; another company in Sljivcica, which is the feature I'm pointing at now (indicating), Sivrino Selo; and the third company in Ahmici. This battalion controlled the road from Vitez via Vjetrenica to Zenica, and the next battalion, which had its headquarters in Bukve and was also part of the 325th Brigade, had its companies deployed in Bukve, Grbavica, Preocica and controlled one of the auxiliary communication lines, which also leads towards Zenica. The forces of the 333rd Brigade in Busovaca of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were headquartered in Kacuni and were deployed as follows: One battalion in Kacuni, one battalion in Sudine, and another battalion along the main road leading from Zenica across Lasva to Kaonik and Busovaca, and their command post was in the village of Grablje. Let me just add that in old Vitez, Stari Vitez, a Mujahedeen unit was deployed, as well as in Poculica, whose strength was about 100 soldiers, and it was deployed there in late January of 1993. In Fojnica, in early 1993, the 310th Brigade was deployed, and one battalion of this brigade was in the area of the communication line between Fojnica via Lucice, Zivcici, Mehuric, and Kacuni. In the village of Dragacici, there was another Mujahedeen unit deployed. Then there were the forces of the 323rd Brigade of the BH army who later were deployed at Bilalovac in late 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Are you saying '92 or '93?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's 1993, that is, late January 1993, that is, from about the 25th of January, 1993 and onward. What is also interesting here are the forces of the 302nd Brigade from the Visoko Operative Group forces. This Operative Group, on orders of the main staff of the supreme command of the BH army, as of the 18th of January, 1993, was subordinated to the command of the 3rd Corps in Zenica. Earlier it had been under the command of the 1st Corps. Unfortunately, here on the model, we don't have Kakanj, but with your permission, Your Honours, I would like to show it here because one of the Kakanj units is significant for us. This was the 309th Brigade in Kakanj (indicating). In the village of Dobrinje, which is on the main road between Kakanj and Zenica, there was a Mujahedeen training camp there. Also in the mountain lodge of Pogorelica, there was another Mujahedeen training camp, and a Mujahedeen unit was stationed there. This was in Fojnica. This is important because there are communication lines leading to Mostar from there, and this is the second communication line leading south towards Mostar and points beyond, so that from Kiseljak, we can go via Kresevo, Tarcin, Konjic, and Jablanica to get to Mostar, that would be one line, and the other line is from Fojnica via Dusina, Pogorelica, and then Buturovic Polje and Konjic, and there is another line which is Fojnica, Dezevice, then Mount Lopata, Blinje, Tarcin, and Konjic, and then from Fojnica via Sebesic again joins the main communication line towards Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: According to your assessment, in January 1993, how much of the BH army in this territory that you described, how many soldiers did it have organised in brigades that you mentioned and how many soldiers did it have engaged towards the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to our knowledge, there was between 29.000 soldiers up to 33.000 soldiers in this entire area, and on the front towards Travnik, it had engaged, that is to say, on the Novi Travnik-Travnik front line, our assessment was that they had about 1.500 soldiers engaged there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At the same time, with the expansion of the units of the BH army across the territory and the communication lines which were of vital importance both for the BH army and for the HVO, checkpoints were set up in January 1993 armed with armed manpower. Where and when and why were these checkpoints set up?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, we very often discussed these checkpoints and what their function was. The points that I'm going to talk about now were not police checkpoints where we would usually see a police vehicle with two policemen supervising traffic on that particular road, these were the classical type of military checkpoint where, on the left- or right-hand side of the checkpoint, there would be several fortification features and shelters with soldiers in combat deployment, and they supervised these control checkpoints, these checkpoints. At the same time, with the deployment of forces in this way at the checkpoints, they were able to have complete supervision over the communication lines, and that meant not only the road but the area on both sides of the road. They were able to control this entire area. The checkpoints made passage difficult, and depending upon the soldiers manning the checkpoint or the orders that they had received, they were able to stop passage entirely along the communication lines. On the 2nd of January, 1993, the Mehuric checkpoint was set up. For the HVO, it prevented all communication towards the village of Miletici and also towards the military positions at Vlasko and Gromila. Up until the 14th of January, 1993, a control point, a checkpoint, was set up in the Vodavod school, which is in the Novi Travnik municipality, on the road running from Novi Travnik to Bugojno. At this checkpoint, in the school building there, there were some 200 soldiers belonging to the BH army there, and the very fact that 200 soldiers manned the checkpoint clearly indicates that their intention was not only to control traffic in the area. Up until the 14th of January, 1993, the 308th brigade launched an attack on the Medenik feature which had previously been taken over by the HVO in the village of Sebesic, and after that they took over supervision over the Medenik feature and another checkpoint was set up at Pavlovica on the 18th of January, 1993. On the 20th of January, we were informed that a checkpoint was set up at Opara again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What communication line is that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the communication line running from Novi Travnik towards Gornji Vakuf, and this is the communication line from Novi Travnik across Ravne Rostov towards Bugojno. The checkpoint set up by the BH army at Kruscica, this checkpoint was set up on the 20th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a good moment, for purposes of the record, to indicate that the green flags are the checkpoints of the BH army, the blue flags indicate the command posts of the HVO, and the red flags are the positions of the army of the Republika Srpska, whereas the yellow obstacles on the road represent the checkpoints; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The checkpoints at Kacuni were set up on the 21st of January, 1993, and were strengthened with a company, reinforced with a company of soldiers from the 17th Krajina Brigade from Travnik. The checkpoint in the village of Donji Bukovci but on the main road running from Kacuni to Bilalovac --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The Vitez-Busovaca-Kiseljak road, that is?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This checkpoint was set up on the 27th of January, 1993, according to the information that I myself received. The checkpoint at Mali Raj, the Sehitluci position, was set up on the 29th of January, 1993. The checkpoint at Bilalovac was set up on the 29th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If you take a look at all these checkpoints and the operative development or deployment of the BH army, what, with this distance of time and the knowledge that you have since gained and the events that happened later on indicate, what was your military situation like, for example, in a possible conflict with the BH army given this kind of situation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If it was the strategic task of each and every commander to ensure communications with the main staff, and that is what it is, in a situation of this kind, we did not have one single communication line open towards the main staff in Mostar under the control of the HVO; and, on the other hand, the army had several communication lines, that is to say, its 3rd Corps, and it was able to use those communication lines for supplying the army, especially after the 12th of January, 1993, and the conflict that took place in Konjic and Gornji Vakuf. In actual fact, this deployment of forces rendered the Central Bosnia Operative Zone divided. It was divided into enclaves. But with the positioning and deployment of the forces of the 6th -- that is to say, the 4th Corps, the 4th Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Konjic and the forces of the 3rd Corps in Gornji Vakuf, it was completely isolated from the supply centres towards the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before we go on to describe the events that followed, we should like to ask our technical service to take a photo of this situation as it existed in January 1993. We can go back to our places and continue the examination-in-chief from our seats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned that on the 12th of January, 1993, there was a real war, a real armed conflict between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO in Konjic and Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what information reached you on this and what it meant for you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We received information on the conflict only on the 12th of January, 1993, and the conflict had probably taken place a few days earlier. But if I may, Your Honours, I should just like to point this out on the map? May I use the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that would be a good thing, at least personally I think that would be more understandable. It would be easier than just looking at the model.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the transcript, the map will be D540.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Will there be an exhibit for the photograph that was just taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I suppose there would be a photograph with a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Later on we're going to receive the photograph, and when we get the photograph, we'll assign it a number. I think that is perhaps the most logical way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo is actually the director for this photograph, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: But the problem is, in fact, that we don't really know what photograph is involved. We will take advantage of the break so that we can determine exactly what photograph is in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The photograph has to be made individual and has to have a commentary which would make it individual. It has to correspond with a point of the comments made by the witness; otherwise, it's just going to be one more photograph that goes with the model. All right. But that's your problem. We will now turn to General Blaskic and ask him to indicate on the map, to show us how the strategy was supposed to be the one of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, how it took it to the enclave and how it took it to the area behind the lines, so that's what would start the conflict. That's what the Judges would be interested in and would like to see on the map.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, for purposes of orientation, I am looking at Novi Travnik and showing the road which leads from Novi Travnik via Ravne Rostov towards Bugojno, and from Bugojno goes on to Gornji Vakuf. This supervision of the road was in charge of the 1st battalion and the 308th brigade of the BH army from Novi Travnik, and at the Ravne Rostovo motel, the Mujahedeen unit of the 7th Muslim brigade. The 2nd and 3rd battalion and the 38th brigade from Novi Travnik covered the road leading from Novi Travnik via Opara towards Gornji Vakuf once again. The conflicts between the HVO and the BH army in Gornji Vakuf included forces of the 3rd Corps, so the forces of the 3rd Corps were engaged in the conflict from Zenica, and the forces of the Operative Zone of north-west Herzegovina from Tomislavgrad, whereas the units that I was in command of were not included in the conflict in Gornji Vakuf. At the same time, in Konjic, the situation was more or less identical. Unfortunately, I haven't got a map here showing Konjic, but if need be, we can put up a map of that area as well.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is Kiseljak (indicating), I am pointing to Kiseljak, and we said that it went via Kresevo, across Blinje, going on to Tarcin, and further on the road goes towards Konjic. That is one direction, which was monitored by the 9th mountain brigade of the BH army with its command in Tarcin and parts of the 105th mountain brigade with its command in Pazavici. However, the conflicts in Konjic were initiated by the 45th mountain brigade from Konjic itself and sections of the 4th Muslim brigade. For us, of decisive importance for the HVO and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, this was extremely important because they shut off the other communication line which leads from Kiseljak across Kresevo to Konjic and Mostar, or from Kiseljak across Fojnica and Dusina and Pogorelica towards Konjic once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In other words, if the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina sets up a front and blocks Konjic and Gornji Vakuf, could you go to Herzegovina for supplies, logistical purposes and so on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we could not do this because the area was under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I should just like to add at this point that not only did we have no connection between the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia with the south, the south-lying area with this deployment of forces, but with the positioning of the checkpoints running from Kacuni via Donji Bukovci, Mali Raj and Bilalovac, a new communication line was opened in this area which represented an air corridor which was about 10 to 12 kilometres wide, so it went from Kacuni up to Bilalovac, and that corridor linked up, operatively speaking, the forces of the 3rd Corps from Zenica with the forces of the BH army and its 4th Corps which was stationed in Mostar, and from April 1993 onwards with the forces of the 6th Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina which had its command post at Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The onslaught that you're going to describe later on on Bilalovac and Kacuni on the 25th of January, 1993, and the creation of this corridor, was of strategic importance for the BH army if it wished to link up its cause?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely correct. It was a strategic goal because with the execution of that goal, they were able to link up the 3rd Corps of Zenica with the 6th Corps of Fojnica and the 4th Corps from Mostar, but, at the same time, the forces of the staff of the supreme command were linked up, which was located at Mount Igman, and very soon after the successes -- these scored, the supreme command of the BH army was moved to Zenica, to the theatre building there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So the conflict on the 21st, Kacuni-Bilalovac, did it emanate from an incident or was it the logical development of a whole military strategy and situation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was not just a chance incident, all the more so as the headquarters of the supreme command decided prior to the conflict to subordinate the operative group of Visoko to the 3rd Corps. This occurred on about the 18th of January, 1993, which meant that on the battleground running from Zenica to Visoko, which is where the battle was to take place, around Kacuni and Bilalovac, one command was created with the command headquarters in the 3rd Corps in Zenica, which was to command this operation, supervise the operation, and this was a combat operations activity. The area was small, but it was a highly significant area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Having described the general situation to us and having given us the logical military development of the events, we're going to speak of events prior to the conflict itself. May I now have Prosecution Exhibit 456/83? This is a Defence Exhibit, and it is Milivoj Petkovic's order. It went to Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca, Prozor, Konjic, Jablanica and Gornji Vakuf, and before we move on to the contents of this order and your comments, can you tell me, what did it mean to you as a soldier that the commander of the main staff is not issuing an order to you as a commander of the Operative Zone but directly to your subordinated commanders in Vitez, Busovaca, Travnik who were subordinates to you in the Operative Zone? How did you interpret this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is how the Operative Zone was structured at the time, because it would have been normal had the order been directed to the Operative Zone command in Vitez. However, here we see that it has three different addressees, and this shows you the level of our organisation and structure, because parallel to the events on the front, we were also trying to transform the armed population into an army, and I believe we needed more time for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to read you this order and what circumstances it was issued under, and I read. The heading is "Avoidance of incidents - Order." "Given the deterioration of Croat-Muslim relations in the past few days, and in order to avert conflicts detrimental to both, I hereby order ..." This was an order from the 3rd of January, 1993 -- sorry, 13th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is of 13th January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: "I hereby order: 1. All HVO commands are required to analyse on the causes of the conflicts on their territory. 2. Immediately establish contacts with the Muslim side and resolve any problems that have arisen through dialogue. 3. Prevent possible attempts by lower commands to resolve the problems that have arisen by force. 4. Whenever possible, set up joint teams with the Muslim side to resolve past or new conflicts. 5. Make joint efforts to clear roads of roadblocks and remove the newly-established checkpoints. 6. Propose that the Command meet at least once a day to analyse the situation on the ground and propose joint measures. 7. Submit regular and emergency reports on the situation on the ground." Chief of staff of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, General Milivoj Petkovic. General, can you tell me, on the basis of this order, does it seem that General Petkovic does not understand the operational development of the situation but is treating these as a series of incidents?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this a correct interpretation in the light of the future insights into the situation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course this is not correct in hindsight based on the subsequent developments, but it is clear that the situation was going in a different direction because we held meetings, that is myself and Dzemo from the 3rd Corps, on almost a daily basis until the end of 1992, and I was in my command post in Travnik throughout this period, even though the headquarters at that time was in Vitez. We tried, through the joint commission, to identify the causes of conflict in Novi Travnik in October of 1992, but this commission stopped working because the BH army representatives from Novi Travnik stopped taking part in the work of this commission. In order to calm the situation down, in January of 1993 we were able to get mediation from UNPROFOR who convened meetings between the HVO and the BH army, and we attempted through dialogue to overcome these numerous incidents and conflicts which were taking place, and I personally thought that a new conflict could break out in Novi Travnik or in Busovaca, and I therefore insisted with the chief of the main staff to bring in commanders from outside, that is, from the neighbouring municipalities. In one of the many conversations that I had, Colonel Bob Stewart told me, "Now, why Novi Travnik again," from which I concluded that he too had focused his attention on Novi Travnik which, in January of 1993, had registered a number of incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, did you follow the order of General Milivoj Petkovic of 13th January, 1993 and attempt to carry out what the chief of the main staff ordered you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did carry it out, and this order was one of the topics of our meeting of the 14th of January, 1993 which I held with all subordinate commanders, and we had a detailed discussion of this order and tried to implement it in full.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would now like to go to another exhibit, Prosecution Exhibit 456/6, and have it placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is your order of 16 January, 1993 at 1140 hours, and it was addressed to a number of units, including the special purpose unit; first, to all the formations in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and then the special purpose units, Bruno Busic, Ludvig Pavlovic, and Vitezovi, additionally, to the Travnik police department and to the 4th Military Police Battalion in Vitez. Before we move on to the body of text, could you just tell us which of these units had the status of temporarily subordinated units and which units were attached to your command, based on what you mentioned previously today?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the list of addressees where it states, and I quote, "To all the formations of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Which are these units?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These are all the HVO brigades in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone which were directly subordinated to me as their commander, that is, the HVO brigades are these units, and they're the integral part of the military structure of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and separately mentioned are the following addressees: The Bruno Busic unit, the Ludvig Pavlovic unit, the Vitezovi, the Travnik police department, and the 4th Military Police Battalion in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On which basis did you issue an order to them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had received an order from the main staff which can be seen from the preamble, it is 01-66/93, dated 15 January, 1993, in which these units were attached to me or subordinate to me for this particular task of the raising of its battle readiness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the local police department have any combat units, since they were put on the list of addressees?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The police department in Travnik also had a special purpose unit which numbered up to 30 civilian policemen, and that was a combat unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The heading is "The Combat Readiness of all the HVO Formations in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone Territory." I'm just going to read you the preamble here. "Pursuant to the order of the Mostar HVO headquarters, number 01-66/93, dated 15 January, 1993, and due to the open and deceitful aggression of Muslim forces all over the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which has caused scores of HVO members to be killed and a number of them to be wounded, as well as Croatian homes to be burned and the Croatian people driven out, for the purpose of the self-defence of the people and the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, I hereby order the following." Now, please, can you tell the Trial Chamber, at this point in time, that is, on the 16th of January, were there conflicts and the burning of houses in this area, and if not, why -- in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, were there conflicts with Muslims on the 16th of January, that is, the question is "yes" or "no," and the second question is why would you raise your units and all the units which were in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, why would you raise them to the highest level of combat readiness?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First, there were no conflicts in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, but the 3rd Corps from Zenica did take part in combat operations in Gornji Vakuf; in other words, they were directly involved with their forces there. I issued this order because, first of all, I had a duty, I was under obligation to issue it on the basis of the order of the chief of the main staff, and the raising of the combat readiness or preparedness of the units, when, in the neighbouring municipality of Gornji Vakuf, fighting was in progress, was a normal and logical military task because Gornji Vakuf borders on the municipalities of Novi Travnik, Fojnica, Vitez, and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Which are the municipalities from your Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, which are the municipalities in my Operative Zone, and it borders on the back, on the south side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the issuing of this order have anything to do with the conflict in Busovaca on the 25th of January?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The raising of the combat readiness and, let me say, the retyping of this order has nothing to do with the conflicts which took place later in Busovaca, and perhaps it is sufficient to point out item 2 where it states that all HVO formations should be made as mobile as possible. This was not implemented as late as 1995 among the home guard units, and it is clear that the order, as it was stated here, was just retyped, that is, typed over, and was not implementable in that area, and it was clear that, even after the Washington Agreements, this would not be possible to have been implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say "retyped," are you just saying that is was basically copied from the order of General Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We were just obliged to type it up as we got it because we knew that we couldn't implement certain things because we were just not in a position to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you believe that the issuing of this order in a combat situation, when, in a neighbouring municipality, a conflict is going on between the HVO and the BH army, was necessary?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We were just being cautious, and this was a necessary step.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you believe that this is a good time, it is fine with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We will take a 15-minute break before we complete the day's work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will resume the hearing now. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, when asked what would Petkovic's order mean, that is, the order of the chief of the main staff, you said that it was clear that he did not foresee the conflict with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but rather saw these events as incidents. Now, tell me, what was your view at the time of these events? Did you, as a military strategist, manage to foresee a conflict with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or not, and what would have been your situation in case of a conflict with Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, my opinion or view was identical with that of General Petkovic; in other words, I did not expect a war with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. My attention was really focused on the defence of Travnik, Maglaj, and Olovo. The town of Olovo had a majority Muslim population, and we provided every assistance we could to keep this town under the control of the HVO and the BH army. Those were our main fronts, and as I said, I assumed that we could expect certain incidents in Novi Travnik, and I did not foresee or could not foresee a war in January of 1993. From this operational development, it also became clear that the forces of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, with reinforcements from the 1st army Corps, which had been organised in the 1st Operative Group, were much better positioned within Central Bosnia than the HVO was, and operationally speaking, before this battle had begun, we had already lost it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why do you say that you have lost this battle based on this operational development of the BH army? Can you say in more lay terms, maybe perhaps by using Exhibit 539, the map which we introduced last week?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. If I can have the map, I would gladly point to the relevant points.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the ELMO maybe. The points Jablanica, Prozor, Konjic, Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please use both the map here on the ELMO and the model in front of you.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm pointing at Vitez (indicating), to the headquarters of the Operative Zone; Mostar (indicating) where the logistics base and the main headquarters of the HVO were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is about -- okay. We can see it now.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All communication lines leading from Mostar via Jablanica are leading to Vitez, branch out towards Konjic, Tarcin, Kresevo, Kiseljak, and Busovaca to Vitez. The auxiliary line is Jablanica, Konjic via Dusina, Fojnica, and then to Kiseljak, Busovaca, and Vitez. The next line is Mostar, Jablanica, Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, and then Novi Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca, Zenica; further, Gornji Vakuf, Novi Travnik, Travnik, Han Bila, Zenica; and Gornji Vakuf, Bugojno, Ravno Rostovo, Novi Travnik, Travnik, Han Bila, Zenica, and, of course, further on to Kakanj, Vares, Kladanj, and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would the General be so good as to show me Han Bila on the map? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, Han Bila is between Travnik -- I'm now pointing at Han Bila (indicating).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Is it marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, but it's very pale, that is, you cannot even see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All these communication lines, and we're talking about the period of January after the conflict broke out, were inaccessible to the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, including the communication line between Kiseljak, Busovaca, and Vitez in the area of Kacuni and Bilalovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, let's look at the Lasva Valley. This is a valley which has its gates, let's say, the entrance and the exit gates, if we just look at the Lasva Valley itself, were you completely blocked, that is, in all entrances and exits from the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, we were absolutely blocked. We did not have a single communication line open.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In such an operative situation, a commander with your professional experience, and I'm looking now in terms of military theory, would a commander in your position ever decide to enter a battle?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, and I do have training in tactical matters, but when I became aware that we did not have a direct communication line with the main headquarters, it was clear to me that we did not have a military solution in terms of initiating any kind of conflicts, and I, therefore, attempted to stabilise the situation by negotiating.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I now have the exhibit, Prosecution Exhibit, 405, placed on the ELMO? I apologise. It is D405, a Defence Exhibit. It's D539, that is the map. The map is D539. I would now like Defence Exhibit 405 placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: According to some, the conflict broke out on the 24th, according to others on the 25th of January, but you issued an order on the 21st of January to your units, and you say: "Establish contact with the competent command of the BH army. "Proceeding from the order of the Chief of Main Staff of the Mostar HVO, number 01-111/93 of 20 January 1993, and with the purpose of easing tensions, I hereby order: 1. Establish contact with the competent command of the BH army in your zone of responsibility and settle all controversial issues by means of agreement. 2. This order takes effect immediately, and unit commanders are responsible to me for its execution." Signed by Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. Can you tell me what the circumstances were, what was the purpose of your issuing this order three days before the conflict broke out with the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was my attempt to calm down the situation and to have all the incidents and all the events in a zone of responsibility of the BH army and the HVO solved by dialogue without the use of force.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: However, soon thereafter, and then again I think a new complication arose and it came from politics, on Sarajevo television and elsewhere, there was a proclamation of Bozo Rajic, the BH Minister of Defence. Can you tell me what this was about and what were its implications?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
