utterances.text: This was an order of the Defence Minister of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Bozo Rajic, in which this attachment of units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the HVO units was discussed and also the attachment of the HVO units to the BH army units on the basis of the territory of certain provinces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did it have anything to do with the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the decision in the Travnik province, which is part of the Lasva Valley? Who was going to be attached to whom and subordinated to whom there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Specifically speaking, in the municipalities of Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez, and Busovaca, all units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were to be attached to the command of the Operative Zone, but all units composed of the refugees or foreigners were to leave this province, and this was to be the 27th Krajina brigade, 17th Krajina brigade, 305th Jajce brigade, parts of the 7th Muslim brigade, and other parts of units that had been brought in from outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the operative situation which you have been describing this afternoon and the relations between the HVO and the BH army, could this order, (1), be implemented, and, (2), how was it perceived by the HVO and the BH army, and did it become a source of another point of mistrust between the two?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, this order could not have been implemented. I did not receive an official position of the BH army, that is, its 3rd Corps, with respect to this order, but I called a meeting of all unit commanders within the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and in the meeting requested --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Excuse me a moment. All brigade commanders, not unit commanders, all --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct, all brigade commanders of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When did this meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This meeting took place on the 16th of January, 1993, in the Hotel Vitez, that is, the headquarters of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. In this meeting, we read the order which I had received from the main headquarters, and I asked that we, first, establish contact with the representatives of the BH army and, second, to wait for new instructions from the chief of the main staff of the HVO and the chief of the main headquarters of the BH army regarding the implementation of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you tell the brigade commanders anything about the possible conflicts with the BH army in a politically electrified situation of that kind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I let the commanders know that they could freely enter into contact with representatives of the BH army and that they could inform them that we were waiting for orders to proceed and that it was our attitude that a dialogue should be continued and that all outstanding issues between the army and the HVO should be settled through agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: From the 20th of January, the soldiers of the Brestovsko and Bilalovac local community, the HVO soldiers, were not in their villages. Can you explain to us where they were and why this was important for the future meeting, the conflict that was to take place later on, on the 25th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the 25th of January, 1993 -- the 20th of January, I'm sorry, 1993, soldiers of the local communities of Brestovsko and Bilalovac, from the area of the Kiseljak region (indicating), were engaged at positions ranging from the main road between Travnik and Turbe towards Paklarevo in the defence of the town of Travnik itself, and that was a regular shift for these soldiers because the municipality of Kiseljak was the protagonist of the defence of this part of the front line in Travnik. On sector 1, the commanders were Ivica Rajic from Kiseljak and Ivica Cosic from Busovaca. So two municipalities, Kiseljak and Busovaca, were responsible for the defence of positions at sector 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did these soldiers return before the conflict to their villages or not, before the January conflict broke out in 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Those soldiers did not return to their villages from the 20th of January, 1993. From that day onwards, they were located at the Travnik front line. There were 200 soldiers there. A total of 200 soldiers were engaged at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what the importance of those two local communities, Bilalovac and Brestovsko, was in view of the conflict that broke out in the municipality of Kiseljak with the BH army forces?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The conflict that broke out in January 1993, in the area of the Kiseljak municipality and took place in the local community of Bilalovac, so this was the local community from which the soldiers had already, on the 20th of January, 1993, left their families and went to perform their seven-day assignment, which was the defence of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the local community of Brestovsko? Was that a neighbouring community?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was a neighbouring local community from which recruits were engaged to defend the Travnik front.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sometime around the 21st of January, 1993, that is, when you issued your order for calming the situation, your assistant, Pilicic, brought you some important information which he got from the locals of Kotor Varos. Can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Zoran Pilicic was from Kotor Varos himself, and he sent me information that the recruits from the village of Katici, which is this village I'm pointing to now (indicating), and the village of Podjele -- it's not on the model but it is a neighbouring village east of Katici -- expressed concern and anxiety over the fact that they had noticed an amassment of troops of the BH army in the canyon or, rather, the Lasva Valley, that troops were beginning to group in that area, and they did not wish to go to their regular shift to defend the Travnik front. They were afraid of an attack by the BH army units, and they had heard rumours themselves where threats of an attack were being made. I was informed of this at our morning briefing. My assistant, Pilicic, informed me of this situation, and I told him that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was our ally and that the recruits from the village of Katici should, by all means, go on their assignment to defend the town of Travnik, to sector 1, that they should proceed to sector 1, and that he should have talks towards that end and to prevail upon them to go and perform their assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that day, you organised a meeting with the commanders of the brigades. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber -- and you may resume your seat -- what were the subjects that concerned the commanders of the brigades from the individual municipalities in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, in fact, this was not a special meeting, it was a series of meetings, and if we look at the chronology of these meetings, there was a meeting from the 14th onwards and on the 21st, they were regular weekly meetings for the commanders who were able to attend and come to the headquarters to attend those meetings. At 2.00 p.m., we had a meeting with the commanders of the brigades, and the commander from Travnik informed me that there was provocative action on the part of the army of Republika Srpska on the Travnik front, the commander from Novi Travnik, Mr. Borivoj Malbasic, who attended the meeting, also informed us of the frequent attacks launched by small groups of the army of Republika Srpska, once again on the Travnik front.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps we could focus on Busovaca and Kiseljak for the time being because they are the municipalities where, three to four days later, the conflict would break out. Let's see what information reached you from there.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The commander, Jozinovic, Nico Jozinovic, reported to me and said that there was general fear amongst the ranks of his soldiers because of a possible attack from the 3rd Corps from Zenica, and he said that they had noticed that the Bosniak Muslims were moving towards Zenica from Busovaca, that they were leaving and moving also towards Fojnica from Busovaca, that there was an exodus of the population. The commander from Kiseljak, Commander Bozic, reported to us and said that the regular shift had been sent to the Travnik front, and that all the convoys moving past Kiseljak for purposes of the BH army were passing through and that there was very good cooperation, and he particularly stressed the cooperation with the command -- with the headquarters of the 2nd detachment of the BH army from Bilalovac where, on the basis of my order, they had signed an agreement on cooperation and mutual activity. This implied mutual visits and an exchange of experience between the commanders in Kiseljak and the commanders in Bilalovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This took place on the 22nd --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Right, the 21st. That is, three to four days before the conflict in Bilalovac broke out.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The commander also told me on that occasion, the commander from Kiseljak, that he was having difficulties with communication lines between the Operative Zone in Vitez and the command there and the headquarters in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us leave the meeting for the moment because it's not vital to the January conflict. But on the 21st of January, 1993, you received information that a new army had arrived in Kacuni. What was all that about? And I'm thinking of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, of course.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I received information that 100 soldiers had arrived in Kacuni. The soldiers were from within the composition of the 17th Krajina brigade, and the 17th Krajina brigade was stationed here (indicating), at the barracks in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Kacuni is on the main road between Busovaca and Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about Katici? You received fresh information from Katici, did you not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Reports from Katici said that new forces were being brought again, forces belonging to the BH army, that they were being brought from Zenica to the Lasva canyon or valley, in the vicinity of the Lasva, Dusina, and Visnjica villages; that is, this region here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In Vitez, or Stari Vitez and Poculica, what information did you receive as to those two localities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I received information that a group of Mujahedeen had arrived and that they were located in Stari Vitez in a restaurant or a cafe bar called Dibek owned by Bengir and that another group of Mujahedeen had arrived in Poculica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 23rd of January, you were informed by your assistant for intelligence work that he had heard on the radio communication lines from the Serbian army, and he sent you some information. What was it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the information I received was that the Serbs expected a conflict to break out between the Croats and the Muslims and that they had decided to keep quiet for the time being, that is to say, not to launch any combat operations themselves along the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Finally, you received information, which you were to realise just how important it was later on, and it was about a convoy which was to move towards eastern Bosnia. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what the situation was like in eastern Bosnia, and what happened with the aid and assistance that the army was to have received in eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The situation in eastern Bosnia from the beginning of November 1992 was very serious for the majority population, the Bosniak Muslim population of eastern Bosnia, and on the 1st of November, 1992, I, therefore, suggested to General Prkacin --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: A little slower, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- to send a battalion numbering 300 soldiers, it was called the Zmaj Od Bosne Battalion, to the Zepa area, and the soldiers were equipped and armed by the Croatian Defence Council, and that battalion went on the 1st of November to that part of the front. On the 23rd of January at about 8.30 p.m., I received information at the barracks in Kiseljak that the greatest convoy of armaments and military materiel had been stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Whose convoy was it and what military materiel did it contain?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The convoy was owned by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was composed of 10 trailer trucks. The vehicles had already been parked at the barracks in Kiseljak for a check, an examination, and there were about 200 to 250 tonnes of freight in the trailer trucks or about two and a half million rounds of ammunition, bullets, two and a half million bullets, in fact. At about 2100 hours, the representative of the defence department called me and asked me to undertake urgent measures to ensure that the convoy not be examined according to standard procedure, the procedure applied hitherto, but that it should continue its route via Visoko towards eastern Bosnia immediately. I undertook measures of that kind and asked the command at Kiseljak to inform me personally once the convoy had reached the area controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina so that I could inform the head of the defence department that the convoy had already been placed under the control of the army. At around 2130 hours, I reported to the head of the defence department that the convoy had been taken over by the escort of the BH army at the Visoko position and that the convoy had continued along its route towards its destination point, that is to say, towards eastern Bosnia. I can show you this on the model. The convoy was stopped in Kiseljak. After the defence minister telephoned, it continued along its route, and at 9.30 p.m., it was taken over by the BH army, and it continued its journey towards Visoko, and it was to have continued towards its destination, eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we say that there was a critical military situation for the BH army in eastern Bosnia in its fighting with the army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was a critical military situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: With the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, what did the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina lack most, manpower or ammunition? What did they need most of all?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they needed ammunition in the first place, and that was their biggest problem. There was not the same problem with manpower.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened with the aid and assistance that could have saved eastern Bosnia? Would you explain this to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That aid and assistance ended up in the main logistics centre in Visoko, and at 2300 hours, I was -- on the 23rd of January, 1993, my assistant from Kiseljak called me up and informed me that the complete convoy was being unloaded in the main logistics centre of the supreme command headquarters in Visoko and that it was quite obvious that it would not continue its route to its destination in eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: After the conflict broke out and with hindsight, so to speak, what were you able to conclude? What was the strategic decision of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army? How were they to use these two and a half million bullets? Was it to defend eastern Bosnia or was it for some other purpose?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Later on and with hindsight, we came to realise, and I can be absolutely sure in saying this, that most of that materiel was used against the Croats of Central Bosnia and not to defend eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 23rd of January, two days prior to the conflict, you left your headquarters and went to Kiseljak. Why? What was your purpose in doing so?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 23rd of January, it was a regular weekend, and I was outside the headquarters. I was in Kiseljak at my family home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it a routine weekend trip, a home visit?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, if I was absent, the head of staff, Mr. Franjo Nakic, was in charge during my absence or somebody else took over for me, and it was a routine trip. I used to do this once in 10 days or 15 days. I would go home every 10 to 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 25th of January, 1993, had you known that a conflict would have broken out on the 25th of January, 1993, would you have left? Would it be a normal reaction for the commander?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. I would not have left the headquarters had I known of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 24th of January, you were in Kiseljak, and you received some worrying news linked to Kostroman. What was the information you received?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 23rd of January, 1993, I was with my family, my wife, in the local community of Brestovsko, and on the 24th of January, I went to church. I was in church from 11.00 to 1.30 p.m., and in the afternoon, from 2.00 onwards, perhaps, I went to a restaurant, I was in a restaurant, and I overheard a conversation about an incident which had broken out and concerned Ignac Kostroman, but they were sort of discussions in a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell us who Ignac Kostroman was and what the stories were you heard in the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Ignac Kostroman was the secretary of the Croatian Democratic Union, and the restaurant where I was located was called Makao, it was on the Kresevo road, owned by Zvonko Markovic, and the stories told at lunchtime was that he had been blocked at the checkpoint in Kacuni, that he was taken out, and that his driver who accompanied him had been disarmed, and he was taken to be shot, but he was saved thanks to the intervention of the HVO forces from Busovaca, a patrol which arrived on the scene and stopped the attackers at the checkpoint. Those were the stories I heard that afternoon while I was in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You spent the night in your family home, and on the 25th of January, 1993, you wanted to return to the headquarters. We have five more minutes at our disposal today. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what that was like? What information did you receive?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that morning, just like every morning that I spent at home, I intended to leave at 7.00 a.m. and to go via Busovaca to Vitez, and when the driver came to fetch me, he told me that the owner of the house in which he lived did not get to Busovaca via Kacuni, and the owner was a taxi driver, his name was Markovic, from Kiseljak. The driver told me that there were probably some problems at Kacuni. I started out with him. We said we would leave and see where the problem lay, and we drove along and reached the Brestovsko local community, and we were stopped there at a checkpoint and warned --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who cautioned you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The reserve formation of the Kiseljak MUP manned the checkpoint, manned that particular checkpoint, and we were cautioned there, and we were told that there had been no traffic from the Busovaca direction the whole morning and that probably the road had been blocked and that we ought to go back in the direction we had come from, and I did return from Brestovsko to Kiseljak, to the barracks there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In Kiseljak, in the barracks, did you receive any more detailed information as to what was going on?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, it was a little after 8.00, 8.00 a.m., it was 8.30 or 9.00, and the commander of the brigade, Mijo Bozic, arrived. I asked him whether he had any information as to what was going on, and he told me that he didn't. We called the duty officer, and he told us that he had been told that the road had been blocked in Kacuni but that he didn't know what was actually happening in Kacuni and the Busovaca area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you try to contact the UNPROFOR representatives and the representatives of the 3rd Corps to clarify the situation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I sent a liaison officer, the liaison officer with UNPROFOR, and my own driver to the UNPROFOR headquarters in Kiseljak. I dispatched them there, it was the UN headquarters for Bosnia-Herzegovina, and my intention was to receive direct information from them about the situation on the road and the events that had taken place in Kacuni. As far as I recall, I'm not quite sure, but I think I sent a letter with a proposal to the headquarters of the 3rd Corps in Zenica. I faxed them from Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did UNPROFOR manage to convene a meeting with the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, UNPROFOR's reply was, and I addressed the letter to General Morillon and Brigadier General Cordy-Simpson, and they told me that they were not at headquarters but that, in the course of the day, they would send in their reply, and sure enough, in the afternoon, I received information that we would have a meeting, that is, that there would be a meeting between Dzemo and I in Kiseljak at the UNPROFOR headquarters on the 26th of January, 1993 at 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you succeed in contacting your headquarters and Nakic, the chief of the main staff in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, I tried to reach them, and I sought ways and means of coming into contact with them, and we succeeded at one point in making contact because there was considerable difficulty in making contact. I informed him that I had been cut off and was in Kiseljak and asked him what was happening in Kacuni, whether he knew, whether he had received any information as to what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did he give you any basic information on the fighting in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He gave me very scant information and said that a conflict had broken out but that he did not have any details as to what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, as I would now like to hand out some documents, perhaps this would be a good time to adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think this is the right time to stop this session. Let me remind you that we will resume tomorrow morning at 10.00. Court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
